extracted.intended_audience: attorneys and practitioners subject to USPTO discipline; USPTO/OED staff and disciplinary bodies
extracted.subtask_description: A USPTO final order applying the reciprocal-discipline procedure of 37 C.F.R. §11.24 to impose a public reprimand based on state-bar public reprimands, describing the respondent's failures, the respondent's opportunity and burden to contest, and the remedial and notice obligations of the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by another jurisdiction (here, public reprimands issued by the Virginia State Bar) pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notice and Order pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 was served; if the respondent seeks to contest imposition of identical discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d), the respondent must file, within 40 days, a response containing all information believed sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1). Failure to file a response may result in imposition of the discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground triggering § 10.23(b)(6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Violation of 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) occurs when a practitioner 'has been publicly reprimanded by' another jurisdiction; the Final Order finds respondent violated 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) by having been publicly reprimanded by the Virginia State Bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO grounds its reciprocal discipline on the fact of the state public reprimands and the underlying state-rule violations (here, Rules of Professional Conduct 1.3, 1.4, and 8.1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Respondent's burden to establish a genuine issue of material fact (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid imposition of identical discipline, the respondent must establish a genuine issue of material fact under the enumerated grounds in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance:
The Notice required respondents to file, within 40 days, a response 'containing all information Respondent believes is sufficient to establish a genuine issue of material fact that the imposition of discipline identical to that imposed by the Second District Subcommittee of the Virginia State Bar would be unwarranted based upon any of the grounds permissible under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).'
Respondent's failure to file a response was a basis for determining there was no genuine issue of material fact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional conduct standards implicated (Rules 1.3, 1.4, 8.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The state public reprimands were for violations of Rules of Professional Conduct 1.3 (diligence), 1.4 (communication), and 8.1 (cooperation with disciplinary authority/accuracy in statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These rule violations, as found by the Virginia State Bar, serve as the factual and normative basis for the USPTO's reciprocal discipline determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific misconduct findings (client representation failures and non-cooperation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Respondent neglected a criminal matter by 'failing to promptly move for a bond hearing' and 'failing to communicate with his client'; in a second criminal matter he 'failed to keep his client reasonably informed as to the status of the matter or comply with reasonable requests for information'; in a divorce proceeding he 'failed to act with reasonable diligence and promptness.' In addition, he 'failed to reply to attempts by the Virginia State Bar to informally resolve the disputes,' 'failed to reply to letters,' 'failed to reply to demands for written answers to formal complaints,' and 'failed to reply to subsequent subpoenas duces tecum issued for the respective clients' files.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These factual failures illustrate the types of practitioner behaviors that support public reprimand: neglect of client matters, poor or absent communication, lack of diligence, and failure to cooperate with disciplinary inquiries and subpoenas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and publication obligations (37 C.F.R. § 11.59 and related)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disposition ordered: (a) Respondent is publicly reprimanded; (b) the OED Director shall publish this Final Order; (c) the OED Director shall publish a notice in the Official Gazette; (d) in accordance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.59, the OED Director shall give notice of the public discipline and reasons to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the State where practitioner is admitted, to courts where admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order specifies exact remedial/notice actions: publication in Official Gazette, posting in the OED Reading Room, and notices to relevant agencies and courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory authority for USPTO disciplinary action
rubrics_metrics.description: This action is taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 2(b)(2)(D) and 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.20, 11.24, and 11.59.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Citations identify the legal basis for USPTO jurisdiction to impose discipline on practitioners authorized to practice before the Office and to carry out reciprocal-discipline procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service and certification requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Certificate of Service certifies mailing of the Final Order to the Respondent by first class certified mail, return receipt requested, to the last address on file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proper service and a certificate of service are required parts of disciplinary process documentation and recordkeeping.
